title: Taxation: Kenya, Nigeria, South Africa, Egypt
note: Corporate and personal tax rates for Kenya, Nigeria, South Africa and Egypt across six headings: capital gains, income and interest, dividends, withholding, corporate, and property or wealth. Every rate carries the source name, the source_url actually fetched, and the as-of year or date the rate applied. Only revenue authorities' own publications (kra.go.ke, sars.gov.za, eta.gov.eg) and the primary statute or gazette they point to were used: no accounting firm, blog, news article or AI answer is cited. For Nigeria, firs.gov.ng and nrs.gov.ng are unreachable from this host, so the Nigeria cells are sourced from the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 and the Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025 in the Federal Republic of Nigeria Official Gazette (No. 117 of 26 June 2025), read on the National Assembly of Nigeria host nass.gov.ng and fetched directly with no text proxy. Where an item could not be sourced it is ABSENT WITH A REASON and no rate is stated. Rates that changed recently are recorded with the change and its date. Fetched 2026-10-12.

capital_gains.headline: 15% of the net gain, a final tax
capital_gains.rate_or_structure: flat rate on the net gain; net gain = (transfer value less incidental costs of transfer) less adjusted cost (acquisition cost plus incidental and enhancement costs)
capital_gains.source: Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA), Capital Gains Tax
capital_gains.as_of: gains accruing on or after 1 January 2015; gains on sale of shares or comparable interests in foreign entities deriving more than 20% of value from Kenyan immovable property, and indirect disposals by a non-resident holding more than 20% of a Kenyan company, added with effect from 1 July 2023
capital_gains.note: Declared and paid by the transferor at the point of transfer. Exemptions include a private residence occupied continuously for the three years before transfer, transfers between spouses and former spouses on divorce, transfers to immediate family, and intra-group restructuring.

income_and_interest.headline: Progressive bands with a 35% top marginal rate; interest is taxed by withholding and is a final tax for residents on qualifying interest

bands.band: on all income above KES 9,600,000 (monthly above 32,333)

income_and_interest.relief: personal relief KES 28,800 per year (KES 2,400 per month); insurance relief 15% of premiums capped at KES 60,000 per year
income_and_interest.interest: interest is collected through withholding tax: 15% on bank interest (resident and non-resident); 10% resident and 15% non-resident on housing bond interest; 15% on interest on government bearer bonds of at least two years (7.5% if issued outside Kenya); 25% on other bearer bonds; 10% on bearer bonds with a maturity of ten years or more. Withholding on qualifying interest is a final tax for residents.
income_and_interest.source: Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA), Individual Income Tax; KRA Withholding Tax
income_and_interest.as_of: tax bands with effect from 1 July 2023; personal relief with effect from 25 April 2020
income_and_interest.note: Non-resident employees are taxed at the same rates but get no personal relief.

dividends.headline: Withheld at source; 10% for residents and 15% for non-residents
dividends.rate_resident: 10% (nil for a resident company controlling 12.5% or more of the voting power; 5% on a resident qualifying dividend and for citizens of EAC partner states)
dividends.withheld_at_source: yes, deducted by the payer and remitted to KRA within five working days
dividends.note: Withholding on a qualifying dividend is a final tax for residents.

withholding.headline: A matrix by payment type and by residency (rate for resident against non-resident)

matrix.payment: sales promotion, marketing and advertising services
winnings from betting, gaming, prize competition, gambling
interest on government bearer bonds of two years or more
rental income tax withheld by appointed agents

withholding.treaty_rates: KRA publishes a Treaties and International Policy section; the withholding tax page does not enumerate treaty rates
withholding.final_tax: final for a non-resident with no permanent establishment in Kenya; for residents, final only on winnings, qualifying interest, qualifying dividend and pensions, otherwise creditable
withholding.as_of: current KRA published schedule; non-refundability of non-resident withholding tax introduced by the Finance Act 2023

corporate.headline: 30% for resident companies; 37.5% for non-resident companies
corporate.reduced_or_small_company: no reduced corporate band on the KRA pages fetched; a Turnover Tax regime applies to resident businesses with gross turnover above KES 1,000,000 and up to KES 25,000,000 (KRA states the regime exists and names the threshold but the fetched page does not give the Turnover Tax percentage)
corporate.sector_specific: no sector rate on the fetched pages; KRA points to corporation tax incentives and exemptions (for example newly listed companies, Export Processing Zone entities)
corporate.source: Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA), Filing and Paying Taxes for Companies and Partnerships

property_wealth.headline: PARTIAL: rental income treatment is sourced, but KRA publishes no stamp duty rate
property_wealth.transfer_tax: Stamp duty is charged on the transfer of properties, shares and stock. KRA states it is collected by KRA under section 2 of the Stamp Duty Act (Cap 480) and that it is payable at different rates depending on the nature of the instrument.
property_wealth.rental_income: Residential rental income (the Monthly Rental Income regime) is taxed at 7.5% of gross rent received and is a final tax, effective 1 January 2024 (previously 10%); commercial rental income is taxed at the normal income tax rates. The regime applies to resident persons whose residential rental income is above KES 280,000 and does not exceed KES 15,000,000 a year.
property_wealth.wealth_or_estate_tax: no wealth tax or estate duty is stated by KRA
property_wealth.source: Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA), Rental Income Tax; KRA, Taxation for Companies and Partnerships (Types of Taxes), for the stamp duty description
property_wealth.verdict: primary (revenue authority) for the rental treatment and the stamp duty description only; the stamp duty RATE is not published by KRA

capital_gains.headline: Inclusion-rate structure with effective rates of 18% for individuals and special trusts, 21.6% for companies, and 36% for other trusts
capital_gains.rate_or_structure: a capital gain is reduced by the annual exclusion and assessed losses and then included in taxable income at an inclusion rate and taxed at the normal rate; SARS publishes the resulting effective rates
capital_gains.exclusions: annual exclusion of R50,000 of capital gain or loss for individuals and special trusts; R3,000,000 gain or loss on disposal of a primary residence; most personal-use assets; retirement benefits; payments under original long-term insurance policies
capital_gains.source: South African Revenue Service (SARS), Capital Gains Tax (CGT) tax rates
capital_gains.source_last_updated: 25 February 2026 (Budget 2026 update shown on the page)
capital_gains.as_of: 2027 tax year; the percentages are unchanged (companies 21.6% since the 2023 tax year, when the rate fell from 22.4%; individuals 18%)
capital_gains.note: Budget 2026 changed exclusions, not the percentages. The governing legislation is the Eighth Schedule to the Income Tax Act 58 of 1962.

income_and_interest.headline: Progressive bands with a 45% top marginal rate; the first part of a natural person's South African interest is exempt

bands.rate: R44,118 plus 26% of taxable income above R245,100
R79,998 plus 31% of taxable income above R383,100
R125,599 plus 36% of taxable income above R530,200
R185,215 plus 39% of taxable income above R695,800
R259,783 plus 41% of taxable income above R887,000
R666,339 plus 45% of taxable income above R1,878,600

income_and_interest.interest: interest from a South African source earned by any natural person is exempt up to R23,800 a year for a person younger than 65 and R34,500 for a person 65 and older, unchanged since 2015; interest above the exemption is taxed at the individual's marginal rate
income_and_interest.source: South African Revenue Service (SARS), Rates of Tax for Individuals; SARS, Interest and Dividends
income_and_interest.source_last_updated: 17/03/2026 (individuals page); the Interest and Dividends page shows the 25 February 2026 Budget update

dividends.headline: 20%, withheld at source
dividends.withheld_at_source: yes, by the company paying the dividend or by the regulated intermediary, and paid to SARS by the last day of the month following the month of payment
dividends.resident_vs_non_resident: the 20% headline is the same for residents and non-residents; foreign beneficial owners may obtain a reduced rate under a double taxation agreement, and SARS publishes the summary of DTA dividends tax rates. Dividends received by individuals from South African companies are generally exempt from income tax, with the dividends tax withheld instead. Most foreign dividends (shareholding under 10%) are taxable at a maximum effective rate of 20%.
dividends.source: South African Revenue Service (SARS), Dividends Tax; SARS, Interest and Dividends
dividends.as_of: 20% for any dividend paid on or after 22 February 2017 (increased from 15%)

withholding.headline: A matrix: no general withholding on services, but final withholding taxes on interest and royalties paid to non-residents, dividends tax, and a withholding on non-resident sellers of immovable property

matrix.rate: no general withholding tax on services; liability falls on the non-resident's own income tax return

matrix.payment: non-resident seller of South African immovable property
matrix.rate: withholding under section 35A as an advance payment towards the seller's final income tax liability

withholding.treaty_rates: an exemption or reduced rate may apply under a double taxation agreement on submission of a declaration and undertaking (WTI, WTR and WTRD); SARS publishes the DTA rate summaries
withholding.source: South African Revenue Service (SARS), Withholding Tax on Interest (WTI); SARS, Withholding Tax on Royalties; SARS, Dividends Tax; SARS, Capital Gains Tax
withholding.as_of: interest withholding from 1 March 2015; royalty and dividends withholding current

corporate.headline: 27% standard rate; a sliding scale for Small Business Corporations
corporate.reduced_or_small_company: Small Business Corporations: 0% of taxable income up to R99,000; 7% of taxable income above R99,000 up to R365,000; R18,620 plus 21% of taxable income above R365,000 up to R550,000; R57,470 plus 27% of the amount above R550,000 (years of assessment ending 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027)
corporate.trusts: trusts other than special trusts are taxed at 45%
corporate.sector_specific: no sector-specific rate is stated on the SARS page fetched; Personal Service Providers are no longer taxed separately and are taxed as a company or as a trust
corporate.source: South African Revenue Service (SARS), Companies, Trusts and Small Business Corporations (SBC)
corporate.as_of: 27% for years of assessment ending 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027; 28% applied from 1 April 2020 to 30 March 2023 and 27% from 31 March 2023

property_wealth.headline: Transfer duty on property acquisitions and estate duty on deceased estates; no annual wealth tax

transfer_duty.rate: R13,614 plus 6% of the value above R1,663,800
R53,544 plus 8% of the value above R2,329,300
R106,784 plus 11% of the value above R2,994,800
R1,241,456 plus 13% of the value exceeding R13,310,000

property_wealth.estate_duty: 20% on the first R30,000,000 of the dutiable estate and 25% on the dutiable value above R30,000,000, after an abatement of R3,500,000; levied under the Estate Duty Act 1955 on the worldwide property of a person ordinarily resident in South Africa and on South African property of non-residents
property_wealth.rental_income: rental income is taxed as ordinary income at the taxpayer's marginal rate; SARS publishes no separate flat rental regime on the pages fetched
property_wealth.wealth_tax: no annual wealth tax; estate duty is the wealth-transfer tax
property_wealth.source: South African Revenue Service (SARS), Transfer Duty tax rates; SARS, Estate Duty
property_wealth.as_of: transfer duty 2027, with effect from 1 April 2026 (no changes from the 2026 table); the 2026 table, with effect from 1 April 2025, first set the R1,210,000 zero-rate threshold (previously R1,100,000)

countries.authority_note: The Federal Inland Revenue Service was renamed the Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS) in 2025. Both firs.gov.ng and nrs.gov.ng are unreachable from this host: firs.gov.ng times out and nrs.gov.ng serves a Radware bot wall. The Nigeria cells below are therefore sourced from the primary federal statutes on a Nigerian government host, the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 (Act No. 7) and the Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025 (Act No. 5), in the Federal Republic of Nigeria Official Gazette No. 117 of 26 June 2025 (Vol. 112) as published by the National Assembly of Nigeria (nass.gov.ng). Both were fetched directly on 2026-10-12 with no text proxy: nass.gov.ng/documents/download/11249 (Nigeria Tax Act 2025) and nass.gov.ng/documents/download/11250 (Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025). Corroborating copies on other Nigerian government hosts were also fetched and read: tat.gov.ng (Tax Appeal Tribunal) and ngsirs.gov.ng (Nasarawa State Internal Revenue Service). The Joint Revenue Board reform page was read at jtb.gov.ng. The provisions were read in the gazette text: the corporate rate at section 56, the 15% minimum effective tax rate at section 57, the 4% development levy at section 59, the individual bands in the Fourth Schedule, chargeable gains in Part VIII, and the stamp-duty rates in the Ninth Schedule.

capital_gains.headline: No longer a standalone tax: the Capital Gains Tax Act was repealed and chargeable gains are taxed under the income tax, at 30% for companies and at the 0% to 25% personal income tax bands for individuals
capital_gains.rate_or_structure: the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 repealed the Capital Gains Tax Act, the Companies Income Tax Act, the Personal Income Tax Act and the Stamp Duties Act; chargeable gains of a company are included in total profits and taxed at the corporate rate, and chargeable gains of an individual form part of assessable income taxed at the personal income tax bands. A small company pays 0%.
capital_gains.rate: 30% for companies; 0% to 25% (personal income tax bands) for individuals
capital_gains.exemptions: disposal of shares in a Nigerian company is not a chargeable gain where the disposal proceeds in aggregate are less than N150,000,000 and the chargeable gain does not exceed N10,000,000 in any 12 consecutive months; sums not exceeding N50,000,000 for compensation or damages for personal wrong or injury are not chargeable gains (only the excess above N50,000,000 is)
capital_gains.previous_regime: before 1 January 2026, CGT was a flat 10% under the repealed Capital Gains Tax Act
capital_gains.source: Nigeria Tax Act 2025 (Act No. 7), Federal Republic of Nigeria Official Gazette No. 117 of 26 June 2025, published by the National Assembly of Nigeria (nass.gov.ng)
capital_gains.as_of: 1 January 2026 (commencement of the Nigeria Tax Act 2025)
capital_gains.verdict: primary statute (official gazette on nass.gov.ng, a Nigerian government host; fetched directly)
capital_gains.note: Exemptions read in the Act itself: principal private residences (section 51), personal chattels (section 52), and the share-disposal threshold in the proviso to section 33 (disposal proceeds below N150,000,000 with a chargeable gain not above N10,000,000 in any 12 consecutive months).

income_and_interest.headline: Progressive bands with a 25% top marginal rate; interest is taxable income with tax deducted at source
income_and_interest.reliefs: pension contribution, National Housing Fund contribution, National Health Insurance Scheme contribution, life assurance premium, interest on a loan for an owner-occupied residential house, and rent relief of 20% of annual rent paid capped at N500,000
income_and_interest.interest: interest is taxable income and tax is deductible at source; interest on short-term securities and corporate bonds earned by an individual after deduction of tax at source is not charged to further tax (Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 51(5)); where the recipient is a non-resident, the tax deducted on interest, dividend, rent, royalty, directors' fees and entertainers' and sportspersons' payments is the final tax
income_and_interest.source: Nigeria Tax Act 2025 (Act No. 7), Fourth Schedule (Individuals' Income Tax Rates), Federal Republic of Nigeria Official Gazette No. 117 of 26 June 2025, published by the National Assembly of Nigeria (nass.gov.ng); corroborated on the Joint Revenue Board reform page (jtb.gov.ng)
income_and_interest.verdict: primary statute (official gazette on nass.gov.ng) and the authority's own reform page (jtb.gov.ng); both fetched directly

dividends.headline: Withheld at source; the amount after the deduction is franked investment income and, for a non-resident recipient, the deduction is the final tax. The numeric rate is NOT sourced here.
dividends.withheld_at_source: yes, deducted by the person making the payment and remitted to the relevant tax authority
dividends.resident_vs_non_resident: for a non-resident recipient of dividends, the tax deducted is the final tax due; a dividend received by a person after deduction is franked investment income and is not charged to further tax
dividends.source: Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025 (Act No. 5), section 51(2) and 51(3), Federal Republic of Nigeria Official Gazette No. 117 of 26 June 2025, published by the National Assembly of Nigeria (nass.gov.ng)
dividends.verdict: primary statute (nass.gov.ng gazette) for the structure; the RATE is unresolved
dividends.unresolved: the dividend withholding rate is fixed by the Deduction of Tax at Source (Withholding) Regulations 2024, to which the Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025 (section 51) refers; the Act itself does not state the rate. Attempts on 2026-10-12 to fetch the Regulations' gazetted First Schedule from a Nigerian government host failed: firs.gov.ng times out and nrs.gov.ng serves a Radware bot wall; the National Assembly gazette (nass.gov.ng) carries the two tax Acts but not the 2024 Regulations; the Kwara State Internal Revenue Service page (irs.kw.gov.ng) lists the Regulations but its link redirects off-domain to a non-government mirror that no longer serves the file; jrb.gov.ng returns HTTP 403 and the Joint Tax Board Personal Income Tax Guidelines 2026 (jtb.gov.ng) do not reproduce the rate table. The only accessible copies are on accounting firms' and news sites, which are not acceptable sources. No rate is stated here.

withholding.headline: ABSENT: the numeric matrix could not be sourced
withholding.rate_or_structure: the Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025 (section 51) provides that where any payment is made to a person, the payer shall deduct tax at the rate prescribed in the regulations relating to deduction of tax at source; for dividend, interest, rent, royalty, directors' fees and entertainers' and sportspersons' payments the deduction is the final tax for a non-resident recipient; a non-resident company providing technical, consulting, professional or management services to a labelled start-up is subject to a 5% deduction on that income, which is the final tax (section 51(8)). The rates for services, royalties, interest, dividends and rent are set by the Deduction of Tax at Source (Withholding) Regulations 2024, whose rate schedule is not stated in the Act.
withholding.source: Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025 (Act No. 5), section 51, Federal Republic of Nigeria Official Gazette No. 117 of 26 June 2025, published by the National Assembly of Nigeria (nass.gov.ng)
withholding.unresolved: the Deduction of Tax at Source (Withholding) Regulations 2024 rate schedule could not be fetched from a Nigerian government host on 2026-10-12: firs.gov.ng times out; nrs.gov.ng serves a Radware bot wall; nass.gov.ng carries only the tax Acts; irs.kw.gov.ng lists the Regulations but the link redirects off-domain to a non-government mirror that no longer serves the file; jrb.gov.ng returns HTTP 403; the Joint Tax Board Personal Income Tax Guidelines 2026 do not reproduce the table. No withholding rates are stated here.

corporate.headline: 30% for companies other than small companies; 0% for a small company; a minimum effective tax rate of 15% applies to large companies
corporate.minimum_effective_rate: where in any year of assessment the effective tax rate of a company is less than 15%, the company must recompute and pay an additional tax to bring it to 15% (section 57(1)(a)); this applies (section 57(2)) to a company that is a constituent entity of a multinational group with aggregate group turnover of at least EUR 750 million, and to any other company with aggregate turnover of N50,000,000,000 and above in the financial year. The Service may prescribe a higher threshold under section 57(2)(b).
corporate.development_levy: a development levy of 4% is imposed on the assessable profits of all companies chargeable to tax other than small companies and non-resident companies
corporate.sector_specific: hydrocarbon tax and petroleum profits tax regimes are set out separately in the Act; no other sector rate was read on the pages fetched
corporate.source: Nigeria Tax Act 2025 (Act No. 7), section 56 (rate of tax for companies), section 57 (effective tax rate) and section 59 (development levy), Federal Republic of Nigeria Official Gazette No. 117 of 26 June 2025, published by the National Assembly of Nigeria (nass.gov.ng)
corporate.note: the previous regime taxed large companies at 30% and medium companies at 20%; the reduced 25% rate mentioned for companies is not in force and would require a presidential order on the advice of the National Economic Council

property_wealth.headline: Stamp duty on instruments and transfers; no wealth or estate tax

stamp_duty.instrument: agreement for sale of real property / conveyance or transfer

stamp_duty.rate: 0.125% (0.1% for loan capital issued for reconstruction or amalgamation)

stamp_duty.instrument: agreement or memorandum of agreement under hand

property_wealth.rental_income: rental income is taxed as ordinary income under the Act; rent relief of 20% of annual rent paid, capped at N500,000, is available to an individual
property_wealth.wealth_or_estate_tax: no wealth tax or estate duty; the previous CGT on property disposals is now handled within the income tax
property_wealth.source: Nigeria Tax Act 2025 (Act No. 7), Ninth Schedule (stamp duty rates), Federal Republic of Nigeria Official Gazette No. 117 of 26 June 2025, published by the National Assembly of Nigeria (nass.gov.ng)

countries.authority_note: eta.gov.eg is reachable, but its English section publishes no rate tables: the income tax law index at /en/content/income-tax-laws lists only 'Income Tax Law No 91 of 2005', whose PDF is an image-only scan with no text layer. The rates below were read from the authority's own gazette PDFs of the amending laws: Law No. 7 of 2024 (personal income tax bands) and Law No. 199 of 2020 (dividends and capital gains). Some eta.gov.eg law PDFs (for example law_no.53-2014, law_no.101-2012, law_no.44-2014) are image-only scans; they were rendered and read as images. Where a rate could not be confirmed it is left absent.

capital_gains.headline: 10% on capital gains from trading securities listed on the Egyptian Exchange; unlisted-share gains taxed as ordinary income
capital_gains.rate_or_structure: residents (natural persons and legal persons) that realise capital gains on trading in securities listed on the Egyptian Exchange are taxed at a rate of 10% on those gains, with no deduction of any costs; the tax base is the market value of the securities less the difference between the sale price or replacement and cost, after deducting brokerage costs
capital_gains.source: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Law No. 199 of 2020 amending the Income Tax Law, Article 46 repeated (bis) 3
capital_gains.verdict: primary statute (gazette published by the tax authority)
capital_gains.note: gains on securities not listed on the Egyptian Exchange, and shares of Egyptian companies listed or not listed abroad, are treated with ordinary income. The published exceptions refer to certain state-owned stakes.

income_and_interest.headline: Progressive bands with a 27.5% top marginal rate and a personal exemption of EGP 20,000
income_and_interest.exemption: personal exemption of EGP 20,000 a year for the taxpayer (Article 31(1))
income_and_interest.interest: interest is taxed as income at the individual's marginal band; the base law's treatment of bank interest for individuals could not be read from the authority's site (see unresolved)
income_and_interest.history: the original Income Tax Law 91 of 2005 set three personal bands (about 10%, 15% and 20% on net income above EGP 5,000); Law No. 30 of 2023 then a new scale, and Law No. 7 of 2024 replaced Articles 8 and 31(1) with the current bands and the EGP 20,000 exemption
income_and_interest.source: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Law No. 7 of 2024 amending the Income Tax Law, Articles 8 and 31(1); ETA, Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005, Article 8 (original bands)
income_and_interest.as_of: Law No. 7 of 2024, gazetted 12 February 2024, applicable to salaries from the first month after publication and to other taxpayers from the tax period ending after publication
income_and_interest.verdict: primary statute (gazette published by the tax authority)
income_and_interest.unresolved: the specific tax treatment of bank interest earned by individuals could not be read from eta.gov.eg; no interest rate is stated for Egypt here.

dividends.headline: 10%, reduced to 5% where the securities are listed on the Egyptian Exchange, withheld at source
dividends.rate: 10% (5% if the securities are listed on the Egyptian Exchange)
dividends.withheld_at_source: yes, the distributing entity withholds and remits the tax to the Tax Authority by the beginning of the month following the month of payment
dividends.resident_vs_non_resident: the rate is the same for residents and non-residents; non-residents that receive the dividends through a permanent establishment in Egypt are within the same charge; free (bonus) shares distributed are taxed at 5%
dividends.source: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Law No. 199 of 2020 amending the Income Tax Law, Article 46
dividends.verdict: primary statute (gazette published by the tax authority)

withholding.headline: ABSENT: the withholding matrix could not be sourced
withholding.unresolved: eta.gov.eg publishes the income tax law only as an image-only scanned PDF (Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005, 71 pages, no text layer) plus image-only amendment scans; the article-by-article withholding rates for services, royalties and interest could not be transcribed with confidence, and the authority's Arabic rate pages are PDF-only. No withholding rates are stated for Egypt here.

corporate.headline: ABSENT: the current headline corporate rate could not be confirmed from the authority
corporate.unresolved: the Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005 gazette on eta.gov.eg states in Article 49 that the tax base is rounded down to the nearest ten pounds and taxed at 20% of net annual profits, with 40% for the Suez Canal Authority, the Egyptian General Petroleum Corporation and the Central Bank, and 40.55% for petroleum and gas exploration and production companies. That is the law as originally gazetted in 2005; the law has been amended many times, and no amendment raising Article 49 could be located in the authority's published amending laws (Law 44 of 2014 imposes only a temporary additional 5% above EGP 1,000,000 for three years; Law 53 of 2014 does not amend Article 49). No current corporate rate is stated here.

property_wealth.headline: ABSENT: the authority publishes no stamp duty or land tax rates
property_wealth.unresolved: Egypt's real estate tax is administered by the separate Real Estate Tax Authority and stamp duty by a separate stamp duty law, neither published with rates on eta.gov.eg; the ETA services guide (second edition, August 2025) is an Arabic-only PDF and the income tax law gazette on the site is an image-only scan. No property or wealth tax rates are stated for Egypt here.

summary.cells_from_authority_note: cells whose source_url is on one of the named revenue authorities' own domains (kra.go.ke, sars.gov.za, eta.gov.eg, firs.gov.ng/nrs.gov.ng): Kenya 5, South Africa 6, Egypt 3, Nigeria 0. All six Nigeria cells are sourced from the federal primary statutes in the Federal Republic of Nigeria Official Gazette (Nigeria Tax Act 2025, Act No. 7, and Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, Act No. 5, No. 117 of 26 June 2025) on nass.gov.ng, a Nigerian government host, because firs.gov.ng and nrs.gov.ng are unreachable from this host.
unresolved_cells: Kenya property_wealth: stamp duty RATE (KRA states the rate varies by instrument and publishes no table)
Nigeria dividends: the withholding RATE (fixed by regulations not fetchable from a government host)
Nigeria withholding: the full WHT rate matrix (same reason)
Egypt corporate: the current headline rate (only the 2005 gazetted Article 49 figure of 20% could be read)
Egypt withholding: the rate matrix (image-only scans)
Egypt property_wealth: stamp duty and land tax rates (separate authority and law, no rates on eta.gov.eg)
recent_changes: Nigeria: the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 (Act No. 7, gazetted 26 June 2025, effective 1 January 2026) repealed the Capital Gains Tax Act, the Companies Income Tax Act, the Personal Income Tax Act and the Stamp Duties Act; company capital gains are now taxed at the 30% corporate rate, individual gains at new 0% to 25% bands (previously 7% to 24%), small companies pay 0%, and a 4% development levy replaces the former education and related levies
Nigeria: the Deduction of Tax at Source (Withholding) Regulations 2024 took effect 1 July 2024 and revoke the 1997 withholding regulations
Nigeria: the Joint Revenue Board issued Personal Income Tax Guidelines 2026 confirming the new bands and the N150m/N10m share-disposal exemption
South Africa: transfer duty brackets changed with effect from 1 April 2025 (the zero-rate threshold rose to R1,210,000); the 2027 table takes effect 1 April 2026 with no further change
South Africa: Budget 2026 (25 February 2026) changed CGT exclusions but left the CGT effective percentages unchanged at 18% / 21.6% / 36%
South Africa: the 2027 personal income tax brackets and rebates took effect 1 March 2026

Kenya: residential rental income (MRI) was reduced to 7.5% with effect from 1 January 2024 (from 10%); the Finance Act 2026 (effective 1 July 2026) exempts REIT transfers from stamp duty and moves the individual filing deadline to 30 April from 1 January 2027
Egypt: Law No. 7 of 2024 (gazetted 12 February 2024) replaced the personal income tax bands with the current 0% to 27.5% scale and set the personal exemption at EGP 20,000 (from EGP 15,000)
Egypt: Law No. 199 of 2020 (gazetted 30 September 2020) set a 10% tax on gains from listed securities and reduced the dividend tax to 5% for securities listed on the Egyptian Exchange
